solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Struck, a Tesla changed course (8)

blocks.note: kept as it is
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
a sailing boat tacks when it changes course into the wind

annotation.surface: A Tesla car swerves and hits something.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car brand, but here it is the scientific unit, abbreviated T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain past-tense synonym: struck here is the verb of hitting or assaulting, not the noun or the sense of being impressed.

entries.clue: Time to interrupt a trial witness (6)

indicatorNotes.to interrupt: T breaks into the middle of A TEST, splitting it

blocks.note: A + TEST, a trial
T is the standard abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: A witness is running out of time in court.
annotation.walkthrough: Trial and witness both call up a courtroom, but trial here just means a test.
annotation.definitionFit: To witness a document is to attest it, signing to confirm it is genuine.

entries.clue: Rug to go around central columns (6)

indicatorNotes.around: TO + PEE wraps around the U
indicatorNotes.central: take the middle letter of COLUMNS

blocks.note: kept as it is
to go is a coy way to say urinate
the middle letter of COLUMNS

annotation.surface: Instructions for laying a rug around the pillars in a hall.
annotation.walkthrough: Rug is slang for a hairpiece, not a floor covering.
annotation.definitionFit: A toupee is a small wig, jokingly called a rug.

entries.clue: Cold air circulating round a festival eatery (9)

indicatorNotes.circulating: AIR turns round to read RIA
indicatorNotes.round: round means surrounding, so C and RIA sit on either side of A FETE

blocks.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
AIR turned back to front
A + FETE, a festival

annotation.surface: A chilly wind blows around the food tent at a festival.
annotation.walkthrough: Cold, then the turned AIR, wrapped round A FETE in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Eatery is a general word for anywhere serving meals; a self-service canteen is one kind.

entries.clue: Ten sheep all worried about a large predator (8,4)

indicatorNotes.worried: the letters of TEN SHEEP ALL are fretted into a new order
indicatorNotes.about: the shuffled letters sit around the A

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
the A from 'a large predator' also goes in the mix

annotation.surface: A flock of ten sheep panics about a big hunter nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty: it goes inside the mixed letters and also starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The elephant seal is the largest seal, a big hunter of fish and squid.

entries.clue: Nutritionist die-casting for an artist (6)

indicatorNotes.casting: to cast is to throw off, so DIE is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: a dietitian is a nutrition expert
DIE is removed from the front of DIETITIAN

annotation.surface: A nutritionist takes up metal casting to become an artist.
annotation.walkthrough: Die-casting reads as a metalworking process; split it into die + casting (throwing away).
annotation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter.

entries.clue: State contribution to Florida holidays (5)

indicatorNotes.contribution to: the answer is a part given by the following words

blocks.note: florIDA HOlidays

annotation.surface: A US state chips in to pay for Florida vacations.
annotation.walkthrough: Florida sits in the surface as a decoy state; the real one is inside its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the northwest, far from the Florida of the surface.

entries.clue: Batting I wrongly claim is hostile (8)

indicatorNotes.wrongly: I CLAIM's letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: a cricketer who is batting is IN
anagram of I CLAIM

annotation.surface: A fielder objects that someone falsely claimed he was batting in a hostile way.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin inimicus, enemy: an inimical attitude is unfriendly or opposed.

entries.clue: Home of William and not Amanda (8)

blocks.note: nor means 'and not'
Mandy is a short form of Amanda

annotation.surface: A house belongs to William but not to Amanda.
annotation.walkthrough: The William is the Conqueror, Duke of Normandy, not a modern man or prince.
annotation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror came from Normandy before invading England in 1066.

entries.clue: Fungi lead to tummy upsets (8)

blocks.note: first letter of TUMMY
to ruffle someone is to upset them

annotation.surface: Eating wild mushrooms gives you an upset stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: Lead to reads as 'cause'; here it means the letter at the head of tummy.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the prized underground delicacy dug up by pigs and dogs is one sort of fungus.

entries.clue: One’s into wine, right, and expensive food (6)

indicatorNotes.into: into means going inside, so the I is placed within CAVA

blocks.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
I is the Roman numeral one
R is short for right

annotation.surface: A wine buff who also likes luxury food.
annotation.walkthrough: One's into wine reads as someone who loves wine; it is I placed inside CAVA.
annotation.definitionFit: Caviar, sturgeon roe, is famously costly food.

entries.clue: Schools ignoring current campaign broadcast (12)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the current's letter is left out of the word

blocks.note: to school someone is to train them
I, the physics symbol for current, is dropped from TRAINS
a campaign or crusade

annotation.surface: Schools skip current affairs while a campaign goes out on air.
annotation.walkthrough: Schools is a verb (trains), and current is the electrical I, not news.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a radio or TV programme sent out over the air is what is transmitted.

entries.clue: Good person eating little for pudding (5)

indicatorNotes.eating: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so ST takes WEE inside it

blocks.note: ST, saint, the usual good person
wee is Scottish for little

annotation.surface: A good person eats only a little dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage a sweet is a dessert course, as well as a candy.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain, sweet means pudding, the dessert course.

entries.clue: Listen endlessly to girl’s instrument (9)

blocks.note: HARK, listen, without its final K
joins the pieces
a girl's name

annotation.surface: Keep listening to a girl playing her instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the mouth organ is one musical instrument among many.

entries.clue: Decreasing support for evening dress? (7,5)

blocks.note: reads as dwindling backing; really a stand for taking creases out (de-creasing)
reads as formal wear; really for making clothes even, or smooth

annotation.surface: A falling-off in demand for formal evening wear.
annotation.walkthrough: Read decreasing as de-creasing and evening as making even: the board supports a dress while it is pressed.
annotation.definitionFit: An ironing board holds clothes while their creases are removed.

entries.clue: Yeoman’s drink containing iron and tea mixed (9)

indicatorNotes.containing: a container holds things inside it, so BEER wraps round FE and ATE

blocks.note: the drink that holds the rest
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
anagram of TEA

annotation.surface: A yeoman's drink, stirred up with iron and tea.
annotation.walkthrough: The Yeoman Warders at the Tower of London are nicknamed Beefeaters.
annotation.definitionFit: Beefeater is the popular name for a Yeoman Warder of the Tower of London.

entries.clue: Fried food is only eaten by pros periodically (8)

indicatorNotes.eaten by: food eaten ends up inside the eater, so IS SOLE goes within R and S
indicatorNotes.periodically: take every other letter of PROS

blocks.note: the 2nd and 4th letters of PROS
kept as it is
sole means only

annotation.surface: Professionals eat fried food only now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: Periodically reads as 'occasionally' but takes regular letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Rissoles are fried cakes of minced meat or fish.

entries.clue: One admires what the bride said afterwards (8)

blocks.note: the bride's wedding vow, I DO
later means afterwards

annotation.surface: A guest admires how the bride spoke after the wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the definition as one [who] admires.
annotation.definitionFit: An idolater is someone who worships or adores.
annotation.definitionNote: 'One admires' is short for 'one who admires'.

entries.clue: Unexpected warmth in rum maidens distilled (6,6)

indicatorNotes.distilled: the letters are refined into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: The women feel a surprising glow from the rum.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'in' is part of the letters to mix, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: An Indian summer is a spell of warm weather late in autumn.

entries.clue: Way soda tastes at first without lime? (6)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letters of SODA and TASTES
indicatorNotes.without: without in its old sense means outside, so S and T stand on either side of TREE

blocks.note: first letters of SODA and TASTES
the lime, or linden, is a tree

annotation.surface: Asks how soda tastes on first sip without a squeeze of lime.
annotation.walkthrough: Lime means the tree, not the citrus fruit, and without means outside.
annotation.definitionFit: A street is a way, as in road names like Watling Street.

entries.clue: Clubs do something American; something we can’t grasp (6)

blocks.note: C for clubs, the card suit
to do something is to act
US is short for American

annotation.surface: Clubs take American-style action on something baffling.
annotation.walkthrough: Grasp suggests understanding, but a cactus is literally hard to grab because of its spines.
annotation.definitionFit: A cactus is prickly, so nobody would hold it with a bare hand.

entries.clue: Youth claims to possess a large sum (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to possess: what you possess you hold, so SAYS holds A, L and ADD inside it

blocks.note: says means claims
kept as it is
L for large
to sum is to add

annotation.surface: A young person claims to have a lot of money.
annotation.walkthrough: SAYS splits after S to take the inserted letters; large sum reads as one money idea, but it is two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Salad days, from Shakespeare, are the green, inexperienced days of youth.

entries.clue: Hotel key one carries in Indian territory (5)

indicatorNotes.carries in: to carry something in is to hold it inside, so DEL and I hold H between them

blocks.note: the Delete key on a keyboard
Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A hotel porter brings a key into Indian land.
annotation.walkthrough: The key is a keyboard key, not a door key.
annotation.definitionFit: Delhi is India's National Capital Territory.

entries.clue: Lover of old paintings backing more of the same (5)

indicatorNotes.backing: backing means moving backwards, so the paintings' letters run from right to left

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
ART reversed

annotation.surface: A fan of old masters keeps backing more of the same.
annotation.walkthrough: Lover of old paintings reads as an art fan; split it into lover of old (EX) and paintings (ART).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an extra helping is more of what you already had.

entries.clue: Be excluded from ridicule? Barely! (6)

blocks.note: to belittle is to ridicule
BE is taken out

annotation.surface: Can one avoid being mocked? Hardly!
annotation.walkthrough: Little means barely in phrases like 'little known'.
annotation.definitionFit: Little as an adverb means hardly or barely.

entries.clue: Ecstasy inspired by mint not whipped cream (8)

indicatorNotes.inspired by: E is breathed into the mixed letters
indicatorNotes.whipped: MINT NOT is beaten into a new order

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
anagram of MINT NOT

annotation.surface: Ecstasy comes from mint, not from whipped cream.
annotation.walkthrough: Whipped cream looks like one dessert phrase; whipped is the anagram signal and cream alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cream in the medical sense, a soothing lotion rubbed on skin, not the dairy cream of the surface.

entries.clue: Air pressure filter (6)

blocks.note: an air is a tune or melody
a third meaning: stress or tension
to filter is to pass liquid through a sieve

annotation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition. Air pressure reads as one idea, but it splits into air (a tune) and pressure.
annotation.definitionFit: Strain means a melody, stress, and to sieve.

entries.clue: Who won’t appreciate one’s trendy jars? (8)

blocks.note: in means fashionable
something that grates jars on you

annotation.surface: Who wouldn't be grateful for someone's stylish jam jars?
annotation.walkthrough: Jars reads as containers, but it is a verb meaning grates.
annotation.definitionFit: Ingrates are ungrateful people, the ones who won't appreciate what one does for them.
annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes people rather than naming them.
